finding.summary: The all-features CLI includes the global Tracy allocation wrapper independently of the opt-in tracing subscriber layer. Without a collecting profiler, the current non-on-demand client can retain allocation/free callstack events. Cargo reuses the same operational binary path for this feature variant and the ordinary default variant.

source_chain.fact: default=[]; tracy_memory enables tracy. The resolved Tracy dependency feature sets do not contain ondemand or manual-lifetime. All-features activates allocation profiling.
Non-test all-feature products replace System with ProfiledAllocator<System> and requested callstack depth100. Unit-test allocator exemption does not exempt ordinary or integration-test products.
SFM_ENABLE_TRACY_LAYER controls creation of the tracing subscriber layer. No corresponding check gates the global allocation wrapper.
Allocation/free operations emit through the Tracy client independently of the subscriber layer. Windows callstack depth is capped at62, so the requested100 is not effective depth100.
The non-manual client state and connection state are distinct. Starting/possessing the client does not mean a collecting profiler is connected.
The disconnected-event guard is a compile-time on-demand feature, absent from the inspected resolved feature sets.
Without TRACY_ON_DEMAND, these paths allocate callstack storage and append serial allocation/free events even while a collecting profiler is disconnected.
The ordinary connection-wait path does not provide the active serial event drain used after connection. Queued callstack/event storage can remain retained before a collector arrives.
Callstack emission allocates storage sized for the requested capped depth. Repeated allocation/free instrumentation therefore adds storage beyond the application's live allocation set.
Subscriber spans and global allocation profiling are separate emission sources. Disabling layer construction alone cannot stop allocator events.

repair.choice: Keep the existing intentional profiling implementation; make the successful whole-tool gate end with a locked/offline default-feature build of the named operational CLI binary.
repair.promotion: Apply only the two reviewed hunks in promotion.apply_patch.txt after checking the production base SHA256. The staged full-script preview normalizes line endings for review and is not an authorization to copy unrelated bytes.
repair.failure_policy: Any earlier nonzero exit returns immediately; no fallback or cleanup is run. If the final default-bin rebuild fails or the gate is interrupted, do not treat target/debug as an operational product.
normal_command_convention: Use the installed default-feature product, or a freshly built/copied verified default-feature CLI for operational work.
Do not execute or copy the shared all-features target/debug binary as normal runtime merely because check-all or tests compiled it.
Intentional profiling uses run-profiler.ps1 with a collecting profiler. A subsequent Cargo command can overwrite the shared binary, regardless of this successful-gate repair.
